title: Pointers and arrays; array-to-pointer conversion
learningObjectives: Explain the language rule and its constraints.
Trace the example and predict its behaviour.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: In most expressions, an array expression is converted to a pointer to its first element. The array itself is not a pointer object, and sizeof applied to an actual array gives the size of the entire array. Function parameters declared as array parameters are adjusted to pointer parameters.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
In most expressions, an array expression is converted to a pointer to its first element. The array itself is not a pointer object, and sizeof applied to an actual array gives the size of the entire array. Function parameters declared as array parameters are adjusted to pointer parameters.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.code: Understanding the distinction prevents incorrect sizeof calculations and helps explain why functions need an explicit element count when receiving an array.

practise.guidedTask: At the call site, data is converted to a pointer to its first element. The function receives that pointer and the separately supplied count; it cannot recover the original array length with sizeof values.
practise.independentTask: Compare sizeof data in main with sizeof values inside print_values.
hints: Write a function that accepts a const int array parameter and a count, then returns the largest element with a documented empty-input policy.
Array-to-pointer conversion is not performed in every context, including sizeof and unary &.
An array parameter declaration does not pass the complete array by value.
